1. Completely Untested Files
`PaystackService` — no unit spec
sections.content:
`app/services/paystack_service.rb` is only hit indirectly via `billing_spec.rb`. The `verify_transaction` and `initialize_subscription` (yearly plan) branches have zero unit coverage.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/services/paystack_service_spec.rb
sections.content:
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe PaystackService do
  let(:user) { build_stubbed(:user, id: 42, email: "user@example.com") }

  before do
    stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge(
      'PAYSTACK_PUBLIC_KEY'        => 'pk_test',
      'PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY'        => 'sk_test',
      'PAYSTACK_MONTHLY_PLAN_CODE' => 'PLN_monthly',
      'PAYSTACK_YEARLY_PLAN_CODE'  => 'PLN_yearly'
    ))
  end

  describe "#initialize_subscription" do
    it "uses monthly plan code by default" do
      stub_request(:post, "https://api.paystack.co/transaction/initialize")
        .to_return(status: 200, body: {
          status: true,
          data: { authorization_url: "https://checkout.paystack.com/abc" }
        }.to_json)

      url = described_class.new.initialize_subscription(user, callback_url: "http://localhost/callback")
      expect(url).to eq("https://checkout.paystack.com/abc")
    end

    it "uses yearly plan code when plan: 'yearly'" do
      stub_request(:post, "https://api.paystack.co/transaction/initialize")
        .to_return(status: 200, body: {
          status: true, data: { authorization_url: "https://checkout.paystack.com/xyz" }
        }.to_json)

      url = described_class.new.initialize_subscription(user, callback_url: "http://cb", plan: 'yearly')
      expect(url).to eq("https://checkout.paystack.com/xyz")
    end

    it "raises when API returns status: false" do
      stub_request(:post, "https://api.paystack.co/transaction/initialize")
        .to_return(status: 400, body: { status: false, message: "Bad plan" }.to_json)

      expect {
        described_class.new.initialize_subscription(user, callback_url: "http://cb")
      }.to raise_error(StandardError, /Bad plan/)
    end

    it "raises ConfigurationError when env vars missing" do
      stub_const("ENV", {})
      expect {
        described_class.new.initialize_subscription(user, callback_url: "http://cb")
      }.to raise_error(PaystackService::ConfigurationError)
    end
  end

  describe "#verify_transaction" do
    it "returns transaction data on success" do
      stub_request(:get, %r{/transaction/verify/})
        .to_return(status: 200, body: {
          status: true, data: { status: 'success', customer: { customer_code: 'CUS_1' } }
        }.to_json)

      result = described_class.new.verify_transaction("ref_123")
      expect(result['status']).to eq('success')
    end

    it "returns false when transaction is not successful" do
      stub_request(:get, %r{/transaction/verify/})
        .to_return(status: 200, body: {
          status: true, data: { status: 'failed' }
        }.to_json)

      expect(described_class.new.verify_transaction("ref_bad")).to be false
    end

    it "returns false on network error" do
      stub_request(:get, %r{/transaction/verify/}).to_raise(StandardError.new("timeout"))
      expect(described_class.new.verify_transaction("ref_x")).to be false
    end
  end
end
```

sections.title: `FirebaseTokenVerifier` — zero tests
sections.content:
`app/services/firebase_token_verifier.rb` is completely untested. It handles auth — this is a security boundary.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/services/firebase_token_verifier_spec.rb
sections.content:
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe FirebaseTokenVerifier do
  let(:project_id) { 'test-project' }
  let(:kid) { 'key_id_1' }
  # Generate a throwaway RSA key pair for the test
  let(:rsa_key) { OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048) }
  let(:cert) do
    c = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new
    c.public_key = rsa_key.public_key
    c.sign(rsa_key, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new)
    c
  end
  let(:certificates) { { kid => cert.to_pem } }

  before do
    stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge('FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID' => project_id))
    allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_yield # bypass caching in tests
    stub_request(:get, FirebaseTokenVerifier::CERT_URL)
      .to_return(status: 200, body: certificates.to_json)
  end

  def encode_token(payload, key: rsa_key, headers: { kid: kid })
    JWT.encode(payload, key, 'RS256', headers)
  end

  let(:valid_payload) do
    {
      aud:  project_id,
      iss:  "https://securetoken.google.com/#{project_id}",
      sub:  'uid_123',
      exp:  1.hour.from_now.to_i,
      iat:  Time.current.to_i
    }
  end

  it "returns the decoded payload for a valid token" do
    token = encode_token(valid_payload)
    result = described_class.verify(token)
    expect(result['sub']).to eq('uid_123')
  end

  it "returns nil for a malformed token string" do
    expect(described_class.verify("not.a.jwt")).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when the kid is not in Google's certificate list" do
    token = encode_token(valid_payload, headers: { kid: 'unknown_kid' })
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when the signature is invalid" do
    wrong_key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
    token = encode_token(valid_payload, key: wrong_key)
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when Google's certificate endpoint is unreachable" do
    allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({}) # empty cert cache
    token = encode_token(valid_payload)
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end
end
```

sections.content: ```ruby

sections.title: spec/jobs/tool_job_spec.rb
sections.content:
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe ToolJob, type: :job do
  let(:user)       { create(:user) }
  let(:conversion) { create(:conversion, user: user, tool_name: 'Tools::MergePdf', status: :pending) }

  it "calls the correct tool class" do
    tool_instance = instance_double(Tools::MergePdf)
    expect(Tools::MergePdf).to receive(:new).with(conversion).and_return(tool_instance)
    expect(tool_instance).to receive(:call)
    described_class.perform_now(conversion.id)
  end

  it "skips already-completed conversions (idempotency)" do
    conversion.update!(status: :completed)
    expect(Tools::MergePdf).not_to receive(:new)
    described_class.perform_now(conversion.id)
  end

  it "skips already-processing conversions" do
    conversion.update!(status: :processing)
    expect(Tools::MergePdf).not_to receive(:new)
    described_class.perform_now(conversion.id)
  end

  it "no-ops silently when conversion_id does not exist" do
    expect { described_class.perform_now(999_999) }.not_to raise_error
  end

  it "marks conversion failed after exhausting retries" do
    conversion.update!(status: :pending)
    allow(Tools::MergePdf).to receive(:new).and_raise(StandardError, "boom")

    # Simulate the retry_on exhaustion block
    job = described_class.new
    job.arguments = [conversion.id]
    described_class.retry_on_block.call(job, StandardError.new("boom"))

    expect(conversion.reload.status).to eq("failed")
    expect(conversion.error_message).to include("boom")
  end
end
```

sections.content: ```ruby

sections.title: spec/jobs/cleanup_conversions_job_spec.rb
sections.content:
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe CleanupConversionsJob, type: :job do
  let(:free_user) { create(:user, plan: :free) }
  let(:pro_user)  { create(:user, plan: :pro, subscription_status: :active) }

  it "deletes free user conversions older than 24 hours" do
    old  = create(:conversion, user: free_user, created_at: 25.hours.ago)
    new_ = create(:conversion, user: free_user, created_at: 1.hour.ago)

    expect { described_class.perform_now }
      .to change(Conversion, :count).by(-1)

    expect(Conversion.exists?(old.id)).to be false
    expect(Conversion.exists?(new_.id)).to be true
  end

  it "deletes pro user conversions older than 30 days" do
    old  = create(:conversion, user: pro_user, created_at: 31.days.ago)
    new_ = create(:conversion, user: pro_user, created_at: 5.days.ago)

    expect { described_class.perform_now }
      .to change(Conversion, :count).by(-1)

    expect(Conversion.exists?(old.id)).to be false
    expect(Conversion.exists?(new_.id)).to be true
  end

  it "does not delete conversions within retention window" do
    create(:conversion, user: free_user, created_at: 23.hours.ago)
    create(:conversion, user: pro_user,  created_at: 29.days.ago)

    expect { described_class.perform_now }.not_to change(Conversion, :count)
  end
end
```

require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe FirebaseTokenVerifier do
  let(:project_id) { 'test-project' }
  let(:kid) { 'key_id_1' }
  # Generate a throwaway RSA key pair for the test
  let(:rsa_key) { OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048) }
  let(:cert) do
    c = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new
    c.public_key = rsa_key.public_key
    c.sign(rsa_key, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new)
    c
  end
  let(:certificates) { { kid => cert.to_pem } }

  before do
    stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge('FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID' => project_id))
    allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_yield # bypass caching in tests
    stub_request(:get, FirebaseTokenVerifier::CERT_URL)
      .to_return(status: 200, body: certificates.to_json)
  end

  def encode_token(payload, key: rsa_key, headers: { kid: kid })
    JWT.encode(payload, key, 'RS256', headers)
  end

  let(:valid_payload) do
    {
      aud:  project_id,
      iss:  "https://securetoken.google.com/#{project_id}",
      sub:  'uid_123',
      exp:  1.hour.from_now.to_i,
      iat:  Time.current.to_i
    }
  end

  it "returns the decoded payload for a valid token" do
    token = encode_token(valid_payload)
    result = described_class.verify(token)
    expect(result['sub']).to eq('uid_123')
  end

  it "returns nil for a malformed token string" do
    expect(described_class.verify("not.a.jwt")).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when the kid is not in Google's certificate list" do
    token = encode_token(valid_payload, headers: { kid: 'unknown_kid' })
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when the signature is invalid" do
    wrong_key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
    token = encode_token(valid_payload, key: wrong_key)
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end

  it "returns nil when Google's certificate endpoint is unreachable" do
    allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({}) # empty cert cache
    token = encode_token(valid_payload)
    expect(described_class.verify(token)).to be_nil
  end
end
